text: Before you open SSMS or write a single BACKUP statement, you need a plan — and a real backup strategy is a decision about trade-offs, not just turning backups on. This lesson plans Overlook's strategy in plain English, on paper, before any code exists to defend.

There are three backup types, and each one answers a different question. A full backup captures every page of the database at the moment it runs — what did the whole thing look like at 2 a.m.? A differential backup captures every page changed since the last full backup, not since the last differential — what's changed, without re-copying everything? And a log backup captures every transaction since the last log backup — can I recover to the exact minute before something went wrong? A full backup alone would technically keep Overlook safe, but restoring only last night's full throws away a full day of real appointments and billing activity. That gap is exactly what differential and log backups close.

Here's Overlook's restore chain, visualized. A full backup runs Sunday at 2 a.m. — that's the base of the chain. Differentials run daily, and each one captures everything changed since Sunday's full, not since the previous differential. And throughout the business day, log backups run every 15 minutes, capturing every transaction since the last one. To restore, you always need the latest full, plus the latest differential, plus every log backup since, applied in order.

This schedule isn't arbitrary — it's a deliberate trade-off between recovery point objective and recovery time objective. The full backup runs weekly, at low traffic, because it's the expensive one. The differential runs daily, which caps the amount you'd need to replay at one day. And the log backup runs every 15 minutes during business hours, which caps acceptable data loss at 15 minutes — reasonable for a scheduling and billing system, without adding so much overhead that it gets in the way.
That's the plan, in plain English, before a single line of T-SQL. Next lesson, you'll stand up the real Azure SQL Database this plan is going to protect.
